newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief says he moving ahead on Iraqi oil deal.
newsitem.headline: UN chief says he moving ahead on Iraqi oil deal.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday assured Iraq's chief U.N. envoy that the United Nations was moving ahead to implement the oil-for-food deal.
"The secretary-general assured Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon the United Nations was still moving ahead vigorously in our efforts to implement the accord," said U.N. spokesman Ahmad Fawzi.

Hamdoon had been in Baghdad for the past few weeks during the crisis involving Iraqi troops entering Kurdish provinces and the U.S. missile response. He saw Boutros-Ghali for the first time since his return.
No further details about the meeting were given.
The oil-for-food plan, which should have been implemented this month, is on hold until Boutros-Ghali feels Iraq is safe enough for him to field monitors to supervise it.
However, numerous diplomats believe that the United States will seek to delay the deal, at least until the November presidential election.

The oil-for-food accord, signed on May 20 between Iraq and the United Nations, allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise funds for its people suffering under six years of U.N. trade sanctions. The embargoes were imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
